USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the July 6 List 1 tariffs in place and finish the already-started List 2 review on industrial/Made-in-China-2025 goods, but do not pre-commit to lifting proposed List 3 from 10% to 25% before the Aug 20–23 hearings close. Reopen a structured negotiating channel now—aimed at enforceable IP, tech-transfer, and industrial-policy commitments, not another May-style purchase MOU. Use the unused $200B list as leverage at the table rather than firing it immediately.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is modestly positive, not existential. The Section 301 record (22 Mar / 15 Jun) still stands: China has not conceded on forced tech transfer or MIC 2025, and the 19 May joint statement collapsed within ten days when the White House correctly judged purchase promises insufficient. That unfinished structural problem, plus China’s matching 25% on ~$34B (6 Jul) aimed at soybeans, autos, and other politically sensitive exports, is a real hit to US interests. Goods exports to China have already fallen from $12.7B (Mar) to $9.3B (Aug), −26.7%, while the goods trade deficit widened to −$75.1B; USDA cut the US soybean-export outlook from 62.3m to 55.5m tonnes and soybean futures had dropped on the order of 13–20%. CNY has weakened to 6.93 (15 Aug), ~9% in the window, which partly offsets the tariff bite. Those are the threat drivers. They do not justify a further unilateral jump to 25% on ~$200B of more consumer-facing lines: US industrial production is still rising (104.0), VIX is ~14.6, and consumer sentiment is only gently softer (96.2). China also cannot match another $200B dollar-for-dollar (US imports from China ~$505B vs US goods to China ~$130B), so unused List 3 is more valuable as a bargaining chip than as an immediate tax. The May episode showed that de-escalating for purchases alone fails; ZTE has already been settled and the ban lifted (13 Jul). Correct stance is therefore near zero on the escalate–concede axis: negotiate without new concessions, hold existing 301 pressure, and let the comment process discipline any later List 3 decision.
key_factors: Section 301 IP/tech-transfer and MIC 2025 still unaddressed after the May truce collapsed
China matching $34B tariffs on soy, autos and other politically sensitive US exports
US goods exports to China already down ~27%; USDA cut soybean export outlook
US macro still solid (IP up, VIX contained) so threat is sectoral not systemic
CNY depreciation (~9%) is offsetting some tariff pressure
Unused $200B List 3 is more valuable as leverage than as an immediate 25% levy before hearings
Purchase-only deal already failed in May; ZTE ban already lifted as a separate settlement

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines). Public comment / hearing process begins.
At Trump's direction, USTR says it is considering raising the proposed List 3 rate from 10% to 25%.
US exports of goods to mainland China fell from $12.65B (2018-03) to $9.28B (2018-08), change -26.7%.
US goods trade deficit widened from -$69.8B (Mar) to -$75.1B (Aug).
CNY/USD moved from ~6.34 in late February to 6.933 on 2018-08-15, about +9.4% (yuan weaker).
US industrial production still rising: 102.2 (Mar) to 104.0 (Aug).
VIX 14.64 on 2018-08-15 — contained, not a stress regime.

USTR will hold a hearing on the proposed tariffs Aug. 20-23; comment process ends Aug. 30. No dates for future talks with China were announced. NRF: broad tariffs will raise consumer prices and retaliation will hurt farmers.
USDA cut China soybean-import forecast 103m to 95m tonnes and US soybean exports 62.3m to 55.5m tonnes; soybean futures at levels where many US farmers lose money without aid.
Commerce lifted the ZTE denial order after $1B penalty, $400M escrow, leadership overhaul and compliance monitors — removing the main non-tariff squeeze already.
